method: Compare HELIOS public UX and internal architecture against current distributed-compute marketplaces, volunteer-compute controls, workload observability patterns, receipt/provenance practices and current UK remote-game transparency standards. External systems are references for missing capabilities, not source-code or asset donors.

examples: human viewer plus canonical machine receipt patterns

findings.problem: The public receipt was a fixed-height raw JSON viewport. It was technically transparent but visually read as a developer console and hid the important route/resource/proof story inside syntax noise.
findings.action: Add a HELIOS-owned human-first receipt viewer with route, task, CPU/GPU policy, work unit, proof class, sink, receipt ID and timestamp; preserve canonical JSON one disclosure level deeper with COPY JSON.

findings.evidence_pattern: Vast and Golem expose verification/reliability/performance state as first-class selection context.
findings.proposal: TRUST_STRIP: provider verification state, verifier status, agent readiness, success/reject counts and coarse reliability. Production values must come from authoritative provider/fabric evidence, never browser invention.

findings.evidence_pattern: BOINC-class systems separate idle/in-use GPU behavior, battery policy, CPU-time and memory/disk constraints.
findings.proposal: ADVANCED_RESOURCE_GOVERNOR: idle-only, AC-only, GPU-while-idle, pause-on-interaction, thermal ceiling, watt ceiling, RAM/VRAM and concurrency caps enforced locally by Desktop Agent.

findings.evidence_pattern: Vast/Salad expose GPU class, RAM/VRAM, resource allocation and availability/ready state before or during workload placement.
findings.proposal: CAPABILITY_AWARE_ROUTE_CARDS: coarse CPU/GPU/HYBRID preference, minimum VRAM/capability requirements, provider availability and readiness without detailed fingerprinting.

VERIFICATION RIBBON: explicit DEMO / UNVERIFIED / VERIFIED / REJECTED states. Production receipt should be able to bind provider_receipt_id, workload/artifact digest, verified_agent_id, verifier identity, timestamp and optional signature/attestation. Raw machine receipt remains canonical.

findings.evidence_pattern: Modern compute systems distinguish preparing, scheduling, loading, running, degraded, failed, stopped/offline and readiness states.
findings.proposal: COMPUTE_STATE_MACHINE_UI: ARMED -> ADMITTING -> SCHEDULING -> RUNNING -> VERIFYING -> RECEIPT or DEGRADED/REJECTED/STOPPED, mapped only from authoritative runtime states.

findings.evidence_pattern: Residential/distributed GPU systems explicitly account for node interruption, reallocation and health variability.
findings.proposal: RESILIENCE VIEW: show retry/reassignment/verifier-reject state and explain that a failed node is not automatically a failed verified work unit.

findings.evidence_pattern: Current remote-game transparency standards emphasize clear transaction content, current state and easily accessible rules/likelihood information.
findings.proposal: ONE EXPLAIN PANEL: game math/RTP demo disclosure, compute independence, selected route meaning, resource cap meaning, proof meaning and revoke behavior in one accessible surface.
COMPUTE PASSPORT: human-readable history with exportable canonical receipts; production can add portable signed evidence while keeping demo receipts clearly non-authoritative.

PRIVACY_MINIMIZED SELF TEST: optional CPU/GPU/VRAM/thermal/network readiness classes and approved-executor compatibility. Report only admission-relevant coarse classes unless the user explicitly opens diagnostics.

anti_patterns: DO_NOT_USE_VISUAL_INTENSITY_OR SPARKS AS A FALSE THROUGHPUT_OR EARNINGS CLAIM
conclusion: HELIOS already has unusually strong internal separation and compute-plane primitives. Its largest public weakness is now legibility: trust, lifecycle, hardware fit, proof and user comfort policies exist weakly or only internally. The next product phase should make those truths visible without turning the game surface into a datacenter dashboard or allowing external providers to fragment the HELIOS visual contract.
